messages:
maria: Quick sync — customer X flagged a blocker for Private deploy: they require customer-managed egress IPs + BGP sessions in their DC. We need to capture exact acceptance criteria before the PRD. Thoughts?
tj: For the PRD we should define two modes: 'managed-egress' vs 'shared-egress'. Customer wants 'managed-egress' with ASN and BGP peering. Do we need to support advertisement of customer-owned /32s or a delegated range? Also KMS + audit log requirements.
kai: Short note: we can expose an on-prem networking agent that runs a BGP peering process and programs SNAT on the appliance. Need to confirm whether they expect us to originate routes or just accept their announcements and NAT. @sam can you confirm network ops constraints?
sam: They expect to originate the egress IPs (they want control). That implies we must accept TA (customer-originated) route advertisements and offer a per-tenant static SNAT mapping. We'll need to define allowable prefix sizes (/32 vs /24) and tie that into our policy engine. Also flag: MD5 auth vs TTL scopes for sessions.
maria: Draft acceptance criteria idea (for PRD):
  1) Support customer-originated route advertisement for configured prefixes.
  2) Bind a static egress IP per tenant with deterministic NAT and preserve source port mapping.
  3) Automated failover: withdraw/announce logic with health checks and fallback to shared-egress within 60s.
  4) Audit trail & observable route-change events surfaced in Console + logs.
  5) Clear contract clause for who owns route origination and abuse handling.
alex: Ops concerns: who owns session maintenance during upgrades and kernel restarts? Suggest we require a heartbeat protocol and automatic reconvergence, plus an operator-facing runbook for session flaps. Also we should define chaos test acceptance: upgrade with active sessions and no traffic interruption > 30s.
deploy-bot: [system] RFC draft uploaded: /rfc/private-bgp-egress-draft.md (owner: kai)
kai: I'll start an edge-cases checklist:
  - overlapping prefixes announced by customer vs global routing table
  - route hijack detection / RPKI validation optionality
  - partial peering (IPv4 only) vs full dual-stack expectation
  - what to do when customer withdraws prefix but keeps SNAT mapping
  - rate-limiting route updates to avoid storms
  - customer asks for BGP communities to control egress routing policy
Please add more.
tj: Test plan (CI + manual):
  - inject route withdraw and validate traffic flips to fallback within 30s
  - simulate mis-advertise and ensure policy rejects overlaps with protected prefixes
  - interop smoke tests against Arista + Cisco labs
  - IPv6 route announce/withdraw validation
  - automated acceptance gate in the install wizard for on-prem appliance
sam: Rough timeline estimate: engineering work ~2-3 sprints to implement core peering + config UX; infra changes to appliance + on-prem installer; update docs & support runbooks. Product: can customers wait for post-1.0 or do we treat as priority-sell? @maria
maria: Decision: surface as 'priority add-on' on the roadmap. For GA we require: e2e test harness, documented SLOs for failover (<=60s), operator runbooks, legal addendum for route origination. If customer wants priority, price as an enterprise integration.
alex: Example config snippet for acceptance tests:
```
peer 203.0.113.5 as 64512
announce 198.51.100.0/32
auth md5 secret: xxxxx
health-check-url: https://health.redwood.example/tenant/123
convergence_threshold: 60s
```
maria: I'll update the PRD draft with these acceptance criteria + edge cases and ping legal for contract language. I'll also tag @sales to check commercial asks. Anyone want to add wording before I lock the PRD?
tj: I'll add the CI testcases and a rough effort estimate to the ticket. :thumbsup:
sam: +1
maria: Thanks all — quick 15m sync in 15 to finalize phrasing and owners.
